findings.body: The diff introduces `turn.round_start` as the bound for `read_pinboard`, asserting that it withholds pins written by round-mates.  The `turn` variable here is an element of the `round` Vec; the old code had no such field.  The lookup for `HiveStep` returned no accessible definition, so I cannot confirm that `HiveTurn` carries a `round_start` field.  If it does not, this line will fail to compile.  If it exists but is not set by the code that constructs the turns (which is outside this diff, in `step`), then the bound will be unpredictable and the isolation contract broken.  The author should verify that `round_start` is a real field on `HiveTurn` and that every turn in the round carries the same correct value.
findings.title: Verify that HiveTurn has a round_start field

value.summary: This change converts the episode loop from handling one turn per iteration to handling a round of turns per iteration, as returned by the new `HiveStep::Speak { turns, next_state }` variant.  The core logic (prompt construction, append, aside, referral) is identical per turn, only moved inside a `for turn in round` loop.  The commit discipline is correctly hoisted to after the round loop.  However, there is a critical semantic mismatch: the diff uses `turn.round_start` to bound the pinboard read, but `turn` in the new code is an element of `round`, and the diff does not show `round_start` being propagated to individual turns or documented on `HiveTurn`.  The lookup results are empty (unavailable), so I cannot verify this field exists; if it does not exist or is a different member, the pinboard bound is either a compiler error or silently wrong.
